newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt to abolish residential property tax.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt to abolish residential property tax.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Thursday that the government has decided to abolish residential property tax with effect from April 5, 1997, the next valuation date.
The revenue loss from this abolition is estimated at 15 million punts in a full year, Quinn said in a statement.
The government has also decided to increase stamp duty on residential properties valued at 150,000 punts or more to nine percent from six percent, he said.
This increase will take effect from midnight on January 22, which is budget day, and is expected to raise an additional 14 million punts in a full year.
